Norwegian
AI-native debt collection company Audun has raised $3 million in funding from
Alliance VC, Y Combinator, Robinhood Ventures, Skyfall, First Degree and angel
investors across Europe and the United States.

Founded
by Peter Flo, Magnus Vonen, Jacob Hambro and Henrik Fevang, Audun aims to
modernise the debt collection industry by integrating AI into traditionally
manual processes.

The
company's technology automates routine case handling, including responding to
common questions and enquiries, allowing employees to focus on more complex
cases that require human judgement. This approach enables Audun to resolve
claims faster and at lower costs while improving the experience for debtors.

Beyond
automating case handling, Audun uses data and AI to help clients identify and
address payment problems before they reach collections, shifting the focus
towards prevention and early intervention.

We
believe AI will mean more payment problems are resolved before they ever reach
collections. In the future, agents will sit on each side of the customer
relationship and solve payment problems together. But that won’t happen by
itself. Someone has to drive that shift,

said Jacob Hambro, co-founder and CEO
of Audun.

These
developments could also have wider implications for the debt collection
industry. Magnus Vonen, co-founder and Chief Commercial Officer of Audun,
believes that faster case resolution and earlier intervention could
significantly reduce the size of the market, putting pressure on traditional
providers to adapt.

Audun
received its Norwegian debt collection licence in September 2026 and now serves
several dozen clients, with new customers joining every week.

The
company currently employs ten people and is actively hiring as it expands into
Sweden and prepares to enter additional international markets in 2027.
